subject: Hands-on routing policy workshop — aligning calendar & prework
messages:
From: Amelia Cho <amelia@orbitai.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@orbitai.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Routing policy workshop request — week of May 19

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo last month — OrbitAI's infra team was impressed with the latency profiles. We'd like to follow up with a hands-on routing policy workshop to lock down model selection, fallback rules, region tiering, and run a short load test to validate throughput for our chat use case.

What we're hoping to accomplish in the session:
- Walk through sample prompts and prompt-class-specific routing (few-shot vs retrieval)
- Agree on primary model variants per region + quantization profiles
- Define fallback chains and cold-start mitigation (cache warming / warm pools)
- Run a short 20-minute load test against a sandbox route to confirm throughput targets

Proposed format: 2 hour workshop (design + policy) + 90 minute hands-on lab (prompt review + load test) — can be split across two days.

Availability window: week of May 19 (PST). Our core attendees: myself (Product), Raj Patel (ML lead), Maya Rao (platform).

I've attached a short prompt sample set and a one-page wishlist to help scope prework. Can your team own model recommendations and a recommended test window for load runs?

Attachments: orbitai-prompt-set.csv (sample prompts), orbitai-wishlist.pdf (one-pager)

Thanks,
Amelia
Product, OrbitAI

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Routing policy workshop request — internal prep

Laura / Priyom —

Looping you in to scope this. Key asks from Amelia: model selection per region, fallback chains, and a short load test in sandbox. Proposed session structure looks good; we should keep the lab focused to avoid scope creep.

Action items:
- Laura: can you prepare 2 model variant recommendations (one high-throughput quantized and one high-quality FP16) with estimated p95 latency at 512 tokens (us & eu)? Put numbers in a short slide (1-2 slides).
- Priyom: please draft a 20-minute load test plan (clients, target rps, warm-up, metrics to collect) and confirm sandbox route name. We should aim for a Canary run with fallback enabled.

Possible slots:
- Tue May 19 09:00–11:00 PT + Wed May 20 09:30–11:00 PT (lab)
- Wed May 20 13:00–15:00 PT + Thu May 21 10:00–11:30 PT (lab)

I can host the workshop and handle policy walkthrough. Priyom — can you also bring a short checklist for KV cache warm-up?

Thanks,
Sean
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Cho <amelia@orbitai.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@orbitai.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 08:52:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Routing policy workshop request — proposed slots & prework

Hi Amelia —

Thanks — we'd be happy to run this. Proposed concrete schedule that keeps design and lab separate:

Option A (preferred):
- Design workshop: Tue, May 19, 09:00–11:00 PT (artists: product + ML + infra)
- Hands-on lab (prompt review + load test): Wed, May 20, 09:30–11:00 PT

Option B (alternate):
- Design workshop: Wed, May 20, 13:00–15:00 PT
- Lab: Thu, May 21, 10:00–11:30 PT

Prework we'd like from OrbitAI:
1) Confirm attendee list + roles (Raj you mentioned ML lead, Maya platform)
2) Mark sample prompt categories in orbitai-prompt-set.csv (Q+A, clarification-heavy, retrieval-heavy)
3) Desired SLOs (p95 latency target, acceptable error rates) — this will guide model tiering

From our side: Laura will bring model recommendations (FP16 vs quantized) and Priyom will bring a 20-minute load test plan with a sandbox route. I attached a draft agenda and the prompt CSV we discussed.

Can you confirm Option A or B by EOD Monday? I'll send a calendar invite once we lock a slot.

Agenda (attached): agenda-routing-hands-on.pdf

Best,
Sean
